selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What does the person think about right before saying “Allah is Most Great” and bowing?
questions.answer: He reflects on Allah’s greatness and on how the sleeping living things and the heavenly bodies are under Allah’s command.

questions.question: What does calling creation “lamps” suggest about the suns and stars?
questions.answer: It suggests they serve a purpose in the world and shine by Allah’s command.

questions.question: What words does the worshipper say as an expression of glorifying Allah’s greatness?
questions.answer: He says “Allah is Most Great.”

questions.question: How are creatures described when their time of service ends?
questions.answer: They are presented like disciplined soldiers being dismissed from duty in an orderly way.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention both yearly and century-long changes?
questions.answer: To show that Allah’s power covers both short cycles and long stretches of time.

questions.question: In what way is the human being supposed to follow the rest of creation?
questions.answer: He is supposed to glorify Allah, humble himself, and prostrate before Him.

questions.question: What feelings should a person have while prostrating, according to the passage?
questions.answer: He should feel amazement, love, humility, and a lowering of his ego.

questions.question: Which character traits should grow in a believer during prostration?
questions.answer: Wonder, love, humility, and freedom from pride should grow in him.

questions.question: How does the passage evaluate the duty of ‘Isha prayer?
questions.answer: It says it is a beautiful, joyful, elevated, and fitting act of worship.

questions.question: Which part of the prayer is being described when the worshipper says “Allah is Most Great” and bends down?
questions.answer: The bowing part of the prayer is being described.

questions.question: How do sleeping plants and animals still point to Allah’s greatness?
questions.answer: Even in their quiet state, they show that they remain under His control and order.

questions.question: What does the image of soldiers under command teach about creation?
questions.answer: It teaches that creation is not independent but follows Allah’s authority.

questions.question: What happens to creatures every year and every century in the image used by the passage?
questions.answer: They complete their service and then pass away in an orderly way.

questions.question: What does this comparison teach about death?
questions.answer: It teaches that death is not chaotic but happens under Allah’s command and wisdom.

questions.question: What season especially shows the return of life?
questions.answer: Spring especially shows it.

questions.question: What should a person learn from the way creation dies and comes back?
questions.answer: He should learn to submit to Allah with humility and to worship Him with awe and love.

questions.question: Why is prostration more than just a body movement in this passage?
questions.answer: Because it expresses deep faith, humble love, and a spiritual rising toward Allah.

questions.question: What conclusion is given about performing the ‘Isha prayer?
questions.answer: It is presented as a noble, pleasant, meaningful, and serious duty.

questions.question: What does the worshipper notice about the world before he bows in this passage?
questions.answer: He notices signs of Allah’s greatness in the resting creatures on earth and in the heavenly bodies above.

questions.question: How are created things in the world presented as serving Allah?
questions.answer: They are shown as obedient workers and troops carrying out His will.

questions.question: What large event in creation is compared to a great prostration of all beings?
questions.answer: The passing away and death of creatures, generation after generation, is compared to a universal prostration.

questions.question: In the passage, what does the death of creatures show about their relationship to Allah?
questions.answer: It shows that they remain under His command and leave their duties in an ordered, obedient way.

questions.question: How does the passage use the image of spring to build hope?
questions.answer: It shows that Allah can bring life back after lifelessness and prepare creation again for service.

questions.question: How is the human being expected to act after thinking about the death and revival of creation?
questions.answer: He should follow that pattern by saying “Allah is Most Great” and going into prostration before Allah.
